floor_history.headline: Recon: engine floor 17 is CHEAT-INFLATED — the HEAD form's volatile-coerced cosA read is not stripped by the sandbox; the honest cheat-free floor is 26, and it decomposes into exactly two independent

Floor 26 -> 13 cheat-free: mechanism A (the cosA lhu+sll16/sra16 shape) CLOSED in pure C by putting an a1[] store between the u16 staging load and its (s16) cast, which blocks combine's fold; build_in

frontier.hypothesis: The remaining 13 diffs are one local-alloc tie-break: angC (pseudo 97, priority 0.25) is allocated late and takes the leftover register, so the register it gets is decided by which quantity claimed $v0 earlier — not by anything angC itself does.
frontier.mechanism: qty_compare_1 sorts quantities by floor_log2(n_refs)*n_refs*size/live_length and breaks exact ties by qty number (creation order), then find_free_reg assigns in REG_ALLOC_ORDER. There is a large cluster of priority-1.00 quantities (many 'used 2 times across 2 insns' pseudos) whose relative order decides whether $v0 is still free when pseudo 97 is reached. No source spelling measured this session changes any of these numbers.
frontier.next_probe: FORENSICS, not structural: rebuild cc1 with the BB2_ALLOC_DEBUG / BB2_PRIO_DEBUG instrumentation named in the s1 ledger (or add a printf in block_alloc) and dump the sorted qty_order plus each find_free_reg decision for the score-13 form. Identify which quantity takes $v0 ahead of pseudo 97 and what would have to change (n_refs, live_length, or a copy suggestion) for pseudo 111 to take $v1 instead. Only then look for a C spelling that moves that specific number.

frontier.hypothesis: The score-13 idiom (u16 staging read + an interleaved output store that blocks combine) is the shared family spelling and closes _SelectSection and hirahira_w_ctrl_2 too — and one of those two may have a smaller residual register gap, making it the cheaper place to solve mechanism B.
frontier.mechanism: All three 3x3 rotation-matrix functions carry regfix rules describing the SAME two mechanisms (the la/volatile addressing block for the cosA read, and sinAxsinB_12 in $a0-vs-$v0). A mechanism present in all three is a property of the original source idiom, and the A half of it is now solved in pure C.
frontier.next_probe: Apply the candidate.c spelling to _SelectSection (10 rules) and hirahira_w_ctrl_2 (63 rules, signature twice) and score each with sandbox --disable all. If either lands with a smaller register-only residue than 13, prototype the B fix there and port back.

frontier.hypothesis: Mechanism B may be sensitive to WHICH store is interleaved and where else stores are interleaved, because moving a store changes the pre-combine insn stream that sched1 and then local-alloc see.
frontier.mechanism: Only two store placements were tried in the blocking slot (a1[5] and a1[0]), and both gave 13 — but no probe interleaved additional a1[] stores elsewhere in the body (e.g. emitting each matrix element as soon as it is computed, which is a plausible original spelling and would rewrite live ranges throughout).
frontier.next_probe: Generate forms that emit a1[] stores eagerly at the point each product is finished (several orderings), stacked on the score-13 form, and score each. Watch build_insns stays 114 and read the angC/index-temp registers with s2/head.py.
